confidence=2.00 scores=[2, 2, 2] reasons=['The description of persistent, brown, greasy-looking, non-removable (and reportedly “peelable” but recurring) spots on the forehead is highly suggestive of seborrheic keratoses—benign epidermal growths commonly appearing in middle-aged and older adults—but other conditions like actinic keratosis, melanocytic nevi, or even fungal infections (e.g., tinea versicolor, though typically scaly and less “greasy”) cannot be reliably excluded without visual inspection, dermoscopy, lesion morphology (e.g., stuck-on appearance, surface texture, borders), distribution, duration, associated symptoms (itching, bleeding), and patient age/sun exposure history; none of these critical features are provided in the text-only log.  
DECISION: Somewhat Unconfident', 'The description of persistent, brown, greasy-looking spots on the forehead that resist removal and recur over months is highly suggestive of seborrheic keratosis—especially the “greasy” or “stuck-on” appearance—but could also overlap with other conditions like actinic keratosis (though typically more scaly/rough), melanocytic nevus, or even fungal infection (e.g., tinea versicolor, though usually not greasy or adherent); however, no information is provided about lesion texture (e.g., waxy, verrucous), borders, size, distribution, associated symptoms (itching, bleeding), skin type, sun exposure history, family history, or dermatoscopic or clinical exam findings—critical for differentiating mimics.  
DECISION: Somewhat Unconfident', 'The description of persistent, brown, greasy-looking, non-removable (and reportedly “peelable” but recurring) spots on the forehead is highly suggestive of seborrheic keratoses—benign epidermal growths commonly appearing in middle-aged and older adults—but other conditions like actinic keratosis, melanocytic nevi, or even fungal infections (e.g., tinea versicolor, though typically scaly and less “greasy”) cannot be reliably excluded without visual inspection, dermoscopy, lesion morphology (e.g., stuck-on appearance, surface texture, borders), distribution, duration, associated symptoms (itching, bleeding), and patient age/sun exposure history; none of these critical features are provided in the text-only log.  
DECISION: Somewhat Unconfident']

confidence=5.00 scores=[5, 5, 5] reasons=['The clinical presentation (brown, greasy, slightly raised, scaly plaques), dermatoscopic finding (cerebriform pattern), and definitive histopathology (hyperkeratosis with horn cysts) are pathognomonic for seborrheic keratosis, and this diagnosis is conclusively confirmed by biopsy—no other common differential (e.g., melanoma, actinic keratosis, verruca vulgaris, or lentigo) fits all features, especially the absence of melanocytic activity on dermatoscopy and the specific histologic hallmark of horn cysts.  
DECISION: Very Confident', 'The clinical presentation (brown, greasy, slightly raised, scaly plaques), dermatoscopic finding (cerebriform pattern), and definitive histopathology (hyperkeratosis with horn cysts) are pathognomonic for seborrheic keratosis, and this diagnosis is conclusively confirmed by biopsy—eliminating mimics such as melanoma, warts, or actinic keratosis.  
DECISION: Very Confident', 'The diagnosis of seborrheic keratosis is strongly supported by the clinical presentation (brown, greasy, slightly raised, scaly plaques), dermatoscopic finding of cerebriform pattern (a classic feature), and definitive histopathology showing hyperkeratosis with horn cysts—pathognomonic for seborrheic keratosis—leaving no reasonable diagnostic uncertainty among common differential diagnoses (e.g., melanoma, actinic keratosis, verruca vulgaris, or lentigo maligna).  
DECISION: Very Confident']
